tom: Quick sync after the QA run — ran into a nasty combo: split-horizon DNS + central egress + dual-stack enabled. Control-plane hostname sometimes resolves to a public IPv6 address and traffic takes a different path, causing gRPC frames to stall.

anika: ugh. do you have repro details?

tom: yes. two resolvers in the VPC returned different answers: the VPC resolver (via dhcp) yields the private A/AAAA, the recursive resolver on our shared egress returns the public addresses. node resolver caching + happy eyeballs means the client sometimes prefers the public AAAA.

rahul: can you paste the DNS outputs?

tom: paste: 
```
; VPC stub resolver
$ dig +short cp.cust-123.rw.local A
10.100.5.7
$ dig +short cp.cust-123.rw.local AAAA
fd00:10:100:5::7

; Central recursive (egress path)
$ dig +short cp.cust-123.rw.local A
3.120.45.90
$ dig +short cp.cust-123.rw.local AAAA
2604:abc::45a
```

grace: any TLS errors in logs?

tom: yes, intermittent TLS verify failures when the client hits the public address then our client cert SAN list only listed private names for that customer. Example: 
```
ERROR controlplane: tls: certificate verify failed: certificate is valid for cp-priv.cust-123.rw.local, not cp.cust-123.rw.local
```

anika: couple vectors here: 1) DNS resolution race (getaddrinfo/Happy Eyeballs), 2) SNAT/hairpin causing asymmetric path and MTU issues, 3) certs that assume private-only hostnames.

rahul: for MTU — we saw gRPC stalls in other customers when traffic got encapsulated through the egress tunnel (GRE/VXLAN). packets get fragmented, gRPC window stalls. Any PMTU discovery happening?

tom: PMTU usually works, but fragmentation + DF=1 inside some snapshots caused blackholes for >1200 byte frames.

grace: options (short list):
- A: Make control plane resolvable only to private addresses inside the VPC (privatelink / interface endpoint). Public names should 302->management console only.
- B: Keep public addresses but implement an egress policy that bypasses SNAT for CP destinations and preserves path (no hairpin).
- C: Agent-level resolver pinning: prefer private RDATA when multiple addrs returned; tweak libc getaddrinfo ordering + happy-eyeballs timer.
- D: Issue multi-SAN certs (include both private and public names) during transitional period.
- E: Delegate a customer-specific zone to the customer (cp.cust-123.redwood-ctls) so they can control internal records.

anika: tradeoffs: A is best for security and predictable path, but requires infra changes and customer infra work. B is less invasive but brittle across routers/NATs and might need provider-specific ACLs. C helps for agent-managed hosts but breaks for proxies and 3rd-party resolvers. D is quick win but increases cert complexity. E is long-term ideal for on-prem cases.

rahul: also consider IPv6-only clients: happy-eyeballs fallback timing is larger than we expect. If the IPv6 route is bad (public IPv6), it can stall the whole handshake. We should ensure we either deprioritize public IPv6 for CP endpoints when in a customer VPC, or remove public AAAA during onboarding.

grace: proposal for rollout:
1) Detect & alert: instrument resolver mismatch and TCP/TLS handshake asymmetric path. Create metric controlplane.dns.mismatch{customer} and controlplane.hairpin_rate. Flag customers with > 0.5% hairpin.
2) Fast mitigation: add multi-SAN certs + agent resolver pin preference for Dedicated/Private tiers. Docs and outbound rules for ops-run.
3) Mid: Console opt-in wizard that creates egress 'no-snat' policy (cloudformation/terraform snippets) and suggests interface endpoint creation. Show risk/consent UX.
4) Long: default per-customer private hostnames and delegated subzone for Private tier (privatelink-first). Hosted stays shared but with improved SNAT preservation.

anika: agree. also add an MTU check in our onboarding probe: test for path MTU to CP endpoints and alert if < 1400. We can add a small UDP probe that simulates gRPC frame sizes.

tom: ops-runbooks: Add checklist for on-prem customers: "If you cannot create privatelink, set up control-plane peering + local DNS delegation and ensure routes avoid SNAT." Include example resolver entries in docs.

rahul: infra changes: ACME hook needs to support additional SANs and automated cert rotation. Also, we should not automatically add customer public names to our cert templates without explicit consent.

grace: agree. UX: console should show a preview of the resources we'll create and require Approve. Mark as "Recommended" for Dedicated/Private.

infra-bot: task created NET-501: "cp-dns-duplication-detection-mtu-probe-and-onboard-wizard" assigned @anika

anika: I'll own the detection spike and the MTU probe. Putting a short doc in the repo.

tom: RahuI can help with agent resolver tweaks (pin private RDATA) and happy-eyeballs timing changes. We'll keep it opt-in first.

grace: I'll draft the onboarding console copy + opt-in flow. We'll surface the risk paragraph about changing customer NAT.

anika: aiming to post spike numbers next Tue. Tom will prototype agent change Wed.

tom: cool, thanks. I'll capture this in the RFC follow-up with the phased plan and link the infra task. Closing this thread when RFC patch lands. :white_check_mark:
